top.h1: Gold you can weigh, check and trust.
top.p: Every piece in our shop is 22K or 18K BIS hallmarked, weighed in front of you, and billed with the rate, the making charge and the GST written out on one line each. Bridal sets, everyday gold, silver for puja and gifts.

collections.h2: Gold and silver for every occasion in the family.
collections.p: Starting prices are for the lightest piece in each group at a 22K rate of ₹9,800 per gram, including making charge and GST. The final price changes with the day’s rate and the weight you pick.

photo.alt: A heavy gold bridal set with two long necklaces, a choker and jhumkas on a display bust

collections.p2: Sita haar, choker, kaan, tikli, mantasha and chur made as one matched set. Order 6 to 8 weeks before the wedding.

photo2.alt: A gold jhumka earring with pearl drops on a woman's ear

collections.p3: Studs from 1.5 g, jhumkas from 4 g, in 22K and lighter 18K.

photo3.alt: A gold pendant with a red stone on a thin chain, worn with a yellow saree

collections.p4: Chains from 3 g for daily wear, with a weight slip.

photo4.alt: Four carved gold bangles with stone work stacked on a dark cloth

collections.p5: Plain, carved and stone-set, sold as pairs. We make shankha-pola with gold caps for brides.

photo5.alt: A kundan necklace set with matching earrings and maang tikka on white cloth

collections.p6: Lighter sets for the reception and bou bhaat. Gold base with set stones, so the weight stays lower than a plain gold set.

photo6.alt: Gold chandelier earrings with green stones and pearls on a display stand

collections.p7: Emerald, ruby and pearl in 22K. Stone weight written on the bill.

photo7.alt: A bride's hand with mehendi wearing gold bangles and two rings

collections.p8: Rings from 2 g. Baby bangles, a tiny chain, or a coin of 1 g, 2 g or 5 g in a gift box.

photo8.alt: A silver anklet with coloured stones on a foot painted with alta

collections.p9: Payel and toe rings, silver pradeep, kosha-kushi, Lakshmi feet, baby bowls and spoons. All 92.5 silver, sold by weight.

charges.h2: What you pay for, and how you know the gold is real.
charges.p: A gold bill has only four parts: the weight of gold, the day’s rate, the making charge for the work, and 3% GST. Wastage is not charged separately. The making charge is the whole labour cost. GST of 3% is added on the total of gold value plus making charge. If you bring old gold, its value comes off before GST is worked out.
charges.h32: MakingHow we charge for the work
charges.p2: Simple work costs less, fine work costs more. The charge is fixed before we start and is written on the estimate you take home.
charges.dt: Machine-made chains, per gram of gold
charges.dt3: Carved and filigree work (jhumka, kaan, pendants)
charges.dt4: Stone-set and kundan, stone weight billed separately
charges.dt5: Bridal sets made to order, fixed after the design is agreed
charges.dt6: Silver items, on the silver value
charges.dt7: Gold coins of 1 g, 2 g, 5 g and 10 g
charges.p3: 91.6% pure. This is what most Bengali ornaments are made in: bangles, haar, kaan, chur. Soft enough for fine carving, which is why the old designs are all in 22K.
charges.p4: 75% pure, harder, better for stone setting and thin everyday chains. Priced lower per gram. A good choice for a daily-wear chain that will not bend.
charges.p5: Sterling silver for payel, puja items and gifts. Hallmarked where the piece is large enough to take a stamp.
charges.p6: Since 2023 every gold ornament sold in India must carry a BIS hallmark with a unique 6-digit HUID. Ours do. Type the number into the BIS Care app at the counter and see the purity record before you pay. We will show you where the stamp is with a loupe.
charges.h37: XRFFree purity check on any gold
charges.p7: Our XRF machine reads purity in two minutes without scratching the piece. Bring gold from anywhere, bought from anyone, and we will test it for no charge and tell you the real karat.
charges.td: Net gold weight <small>Weighed in front of you</small>
charges.td3: 22K rate on the day <small>Example rate for this bill</small>
charges.note: Card EMI of 3, 6 or 9 months is available on bills above ₹25,000. Payments above ₹2 lakh need a PAN card by law.

exchange.h2: Four steps, all of them in front of you.

items.p: On a digital scale that is checked every month. You see the number on the display, not on a slip.
On the XRF machine, not on a touchstone. Old 22K often reads 21K; you get the real value, not a guess.
By weight only. Nothing else is deducted on gold bought from us. On gold from other shops, 2% to 4% for melting loss.

items.h3: The value goes on your bill
items.p: At the day’s rate, before GST. Or take it as cash if the gold was bought here with a bill.

photo.alt: Old carved gold bangles on a bride's hands with mehndi
A gold pendant with red and green stones next to beaded bangles on a brown cloth

scheme.p: Choose a monthly amount from ₹2,000 to ₹25,000. Pay it for 11 months at the counter or by UPI. In the 12th month we add one full instalment from our side. Use the total on any gold jewellery in the shop at that day’s rate.
scheme.p2: The shop’s share is given as a discount on jewellery, not as cash. If you stop early, you get back what you paid, in jewellery, with making charge. A passbook is given on the first payment, and a WhatsApp message on every one after that.
scheme.caption: Example at ₹5,000 a month. The same table works for any amount from ₹2,000 to ₹25,000.

story.h2: Forty years on Rash Behari Avenue.
story.p: Swarnalata Jewellers was opened in 1984 by Nirmal Chandra Dutta, a goldsmith from Sinthee who had made ornaments for other shops for twenty years before he put his own name on a board. His son and daughter-in-law run the shop today. Four of our karigars have been with us for more than fifteen years.
story.p2: We are a small shop and we like it that way. You sit, you are shown pieces one at a time, and nobody hurries you. Every price is worked out on paper in front of you: weight, rate, making charge, GST. If you want to come back the next day with your mother, the piece will be kept aside.

photo.alt: A karigar's hands working on a gold piece under a lamp in the workshop
A gold pendant being soldered with a small torch on the workshop bench

faq.kicker: Questions people ask at the counter

items.p: Yes. Bring a photo or a drawing. Our karigars will tell you the weight it will come to and the making charge, and we fix the price before work starts. Most made-to-order pieces take 2 to 4 weeks; bridal sets take 6 to 8.

Repairs on gold bought from us are free for the first year, except for lost stones. After that we charge only for the work. Pieces from other shops are repaired at a small charge after a purity check.
Yes. Gold bought here with a bill is bought back at the day’s rate with no deduction except stone weight. Gold from elsewhere is bought after an XRF test with 2% to 4% deducted for melting.
Cash, UPI, debit and credit cards, bank transfer. Card EMI of 3, 6 or 9 months on bills above ₹25,000. Payments above ₹2 lakh need a PAN card by law.
For made-to-order pieces the rate is fixed on the day you pay the advance, whichever way the market moves. For ready pieces the price is the rate on the day you buy.
For bridal orders above ₹3 lakh, yes, within Kolkata. Call a week ahead. For everything else we would rather you come to the shop, where the light and the scale are.

items.p: My mother bought her wedding chur here in 1989. We went back for my daughter’s set last winter. They showed us the bill on paper before we agreed to anything, and the weight was exactly what was written.
I put ₹5,000 a month into the scheme for my son’s annaprashan. The passbook was simple, and when the day came the 12th month was added without my asking. Bought a chain and a coin.
